newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWEDEN BOLSTERS CEN BANK, PAVES WAY FOR EMU.
newsitem.headline: SWEDEN BOLSTERS CEN BANK, PAVES WAY FOR EMU.

text.p: Sweden on Tuesday announced measures to reinforce the independence of its central bank, the Riksbank, paving the way for membership of Europe's single currency if it decides to join.

Although Stockholm is seen leaning towards rejection of joining European Monetary Union (EMU), Tuesday's announcement strengthens the central bank's position, giving it a new management structure and transferring foreign exchange policies to the government from the Riksbank.

"This is very positive," Carl B Hamilton, chief economist at Handelsbanken, told Reuters. "It strengthens Swedish inflation policies' long term stability. It's in line with what happened with the Bank of England."
The measures mean an adjustment to phase two of EMU, which Sweden is bound to carry out as a member of the European Union (EU), the ministry said in a statement.
"The agreement, however, does not mean that a position has been taken on whether Sweden should or should not join the European Monetary Union," Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said.
"The measures are of such a nature that they must be carried out regardless of the decision on the EMU issue."
The ruling Social Democrats have said that they will announce their view on EMU in May or June. A party congress will take a final decision in the autumn.

The string of measures are based on a five-party agreement. "The agreement will strengthen the Riksbank's independence and will increase confidence in Swedish monetary and foreign exchange policies," Asbrink said.
To improve confidence in monetary policy, the ministry proposed to enshrine the Riksbank's price stability target in law.

"In addition, without prejudice to the objective of price stability, the Riksbank shall support the general economic policy with the purpose of promoting long-term growth and a high level of employment," the ministry said.

The ministry also proposed a new rule prohibiting all authorities from giving instructions to the Riksbank on matters pertaining to monetary policy and stregthens the central bank governor's position.
"The governor may be relieved from office only if he no longer fulfils the conditions required for the performance of his duties or if he has been guilty of serious misconduct," the ministry said.

However the government stopped short of granting the central bank total independence, saying the governor will have to inform the finance minister before all important monetary and foreign exchange decisions are made, the ministry said.

Furthermore, the Riksbank will get a new management structure, with a governing board supervising a directorate which will be the bank's operating management with responsiblity for all monetary decisions.
The government will take over decisions regarding foreign exchange systems, the ministry said.
"In line with what is applied in other member states of the European Union, the government shall determine the foreign exchange system in the future," the Ministry said.
"The Riksbank shall determine the central rate and fluctuation margins in a system with a fixed exchange rate and manage a floating exchange rate regime."
